doc.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

title: The Merry Makers Twine, Devil Jazz and singing with Oliver's band
summary: The Twine was a chorus dance number, as was Devil Jazz. Mary sang anything with Joe's band, verse and choruses, including A Good Man Is Hard to Find.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Oh, I wanted to ask you again to interrupt you. Oh, excuse me. The New Orleans, I mean the twist, Mary... 된 stuff with
twist. Twine. Was that a dance sort of? Yes, it was a dance. Everywhere they had a movement to it.
The chorus did that. It kind of descriptive thing. Yes. And the Devil Jazz, we had another number, the Devil Jazz. That was a number where the chorus, for every line that you do they
done the step for it. Yes. Of course. We didn't record that one though. I got done. I had every night, we didn't record.

So many good songs. Oh, I used to sing everything. Yes, I used to sing everything. With Joe's band, just anything they'd play, you know. Some of our music and... All the late popular songs, anything that they'd... Anything, yes. They'd play... And you'd sing a vocal chorus or two. Yes. Then you didn't sing just the vocal chorus, you sung the verse too. The verse too, yes. The verse and the chorus. You sing the verse and then you go on

with choruses, many choruses. Yes. At that time, such songs as A Good Man is Hard to Find, that was popular. Mm-hmm. And All Night Long, you know what I mean? Yes. Yes, I have the music. And it isn't what he's got that makes me love him,
it's the way he does. It isn't what he does that makes me love him, it's the way he does it. Yeah. And all those kind of numbers.
